summary: Steve Grothoff continues the Galatians series in 3:26-4:7, moving from justification to adoption. Believing facts about Jesus is not the same as believing in him, and God is not only our judge but our Father who adopted us. Baptized into Christ, we have put on Christ, all are one in him, and so we are heirs according to the promise. The law was a tutor until the fullness of time. The first gift of the inheritance is the Holy Spirit, and the inheritance itself is imperishable, unfading and kept in heaven: eternal life with God.
takeaways: God is not only our judge who acquits us; he is our Father who adopted us and loves us personally.
There is a difference between believing facts about Jesus and believing in him; even Satan agrees with much that is true.
In Christ there is no distinction between believers, so petty divisions over preferences should not separate God's family.
The law was a tutor until Christ came; as heirs we now have the Holy Spirit and his fruit guiding us.
Our inheritance is imperishable, unfading and kept in heaven, so we fix our eyes on what is eternal and live to glorify him.
